organizations.normalization_notes: The historical firm name is preserved exactly; no modern successor is asserted.
ONI is modeled as a military organization. Civilian employment and military assignment at ONI remain separate relationship types.

affiliations.date_precision: documented appearance on 2 December 1940; employment start and end dates not stated
affiliations.research_notes: A contemporary federal decision names Ralph G. Albrecht as counsel through the firm. A scholarly OSS history independently describes Ralph Albrecht as a prominent prewar attorney and places him in wartime ONI and OSS work. The firm is therefore the best-supported last documented civilian employer, not a proven immediate predecessor.

affiliations.role_title: Officer assigned to ONI; prisoner-interrogation and radio-warfare work
affiliations.date_precision: year reported for mission to Great Britain; assignment boundaries not stated
affiliations.research_notes: The scholarly source calls Albrecht an OSS officer assigned to ONI and says he was originally sent to Britain for ONI in 1942. It does not establish whether ONI immediately preceded OSS or overlapped it, and its lieutenant-colonel wording conflicts with the index's lieutenant-commander abbreviation.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Technical Sergeant Cecil V. Albertsen probably represents the man of that exact name listed on a Ritchie Boys roster and later in official diplomatic records.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A curated Ritchie Boys roster prints the exact uncommon name, while a contemporary directory and the Congressional Record document later U.S. diplomatic service under the same full name.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact uncommon name, Army training context, and two independent postwar federal-service references support a probable identity. No service identifier or direct personnel-file link was available.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Ritchie roster is wartime context but supplies no date or OSS chronology; the diplomatic records are postwar and cannot establish pre-OSS employment.
claims.match_notes: The identity remains qualified, and no employer or immediate affiliation is inferred from the Ritchie Boys roster.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Ralph G. Albrecht is very likely the New York attorney, wartime ONI and OSS officer, and Nuremberg prosecutor documented in the cited sources.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Ralph G. Albrecht, of New York City, of counsel
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A 1940 federal decision names attorney Ralph G. Albrecht; Harvard records the same full name at Nuremberg; and a scholarly history links attorney Ralph Albrecht to ONI, OSS, and Nuremberg.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact middle-initial form, legal profession, Nuremberg role, and linked ONI/OSS chronology provide multiple corroborating identifiers beyond the name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources span a documented 1940 legal appearance, wartime ONI and OSS activity beginning by 1942, and the 1945-46 Nuremberg prosecution.
claims.match_notes: The identity is high confidence rather than confirmed because no private identifier or direct personnel-file citation was available, and the scholarly lieutenant-colonel wording conflicts with the index's lieutenant-commander abbreviation.
